content.comment_body: Hello, I'm wondering if it's possible to connect a printer (Ethernet, USB, parallel, or serial) and have it print a timestamp label when triggered by a logic event in my [product_name] setup. I came across an older forum discussion ([url]), but I'm not sure if anyone found a solution. If anyone knows of a new approach, please let me know. Thanks for your help. Best regards, [user_name]
Directly printing labels from a [product_name] is not supported.
Understood, thank you for clarifying. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users explored the possibility of triggering label printing from a [product_name] device. The main limitation highlighted was the absence of built-in or official support for connecting and printing via typical interfaces like Ethernet, USB, parallel, or serial ports based on programmable logic events. This impacts users who are seeking automated label printing as part of their workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to have direct functionality within the [product_name] system to automate sending print jobs to label printers over standard connection interfaces, enabling seamless workflow automation.
